The code prioritizes survival by using strict thresholds to switch to safe options ('a1' or 'a4') when n1 rises, and leverages the default choice (x.n5) only in low-risk scenarios to optimize for reward without unnecessary risk.
This code tightens the safety margins by initiating retreat at lower n1 thresholds (80 and 95) to prevent accidental death, ensuring the agent prioritizes survival over reward in high-risk scenarios.

This code prioritizes survival by raising the threshold for risky actions ($a2$) and using historical data to detect increasing danger trends, ensuring the agent stays alive longer by avoiding high-risk scenarios even when they seem safe in isolation.

This code prioritizes survival by strictly enforcing lower thresholds for safe options ('a1') and stops ('a4') as danger (n1) increases, while using a small history check in the low-risk zone to avoid repeating actions that previously spiked n1.
